newsitem.title: UK: RUGBY UNION-PEACE BREAKS OUT IN ENGLISH RUGBY.
newsitem.headline: RUGBY UNION-PEACE BREAKS OUT IN ENGLISH RUGBY.

text.p: English rugby's year-long feud finally ended on Wednesday when the Rugby Football Union (RFU) and the leading clubs reached an agreement over the future of the domestic game.
Details of the accord will not be published until next week, but the breakthrough ends the threat of England fielding a weakened team in this season's Five Nations championship.

The dispute, which has centred around the clubs' need for money to finance the extra costs associated with a professional sport, has led to England players being withdrawn from national training sessions and touring sides facing below-strength divisional opposition.

The distribution of television rights, players' contracts, the release of players for England and control over domestic competitions and the structure of the season have also been divisive issues, with the clubs threatening to break away from the union on more than one occasion.
When the game went professional in August 1995, the rich clubs were immediately keen to run their own affairs, but the RFU insisted on retaining control.
Cliff Brittle, chairman of the RFU executive committee, has frequently been accused by the clubs of blocking a settlement, but even he now seems satisfied.
"After months of negotiations we have finally reached a fair agreement and one which....will put English rugby in a strong position to face the future," he said.

Donald Kerr, chairman of the organisation representing the clubs, had admitted earlier in the day the patience of both sides had become exhausted. "We just want to get it over. It has been a nightmare," he said.

England players, who face the New Zealand Barbarians on Saturday at Twickenham, are now in a position to sign their international contracts worth up to 70,000 pounds ($117,000) for ever-present members of the side.
All Black coach John Hart had described the dispute on Wednesday as "a cancer in the game" after his side beat a drastiically weakened North side 86-0 last weekend.
